https://iberonews.com/not_det.php?lang=e.text: Taiwan Children’s Choirs Garner Major Awards at Hungarian Choral Competition TAIPEI, Taiwan (Business Wire) Texto completo a continuación 23/07/2026 - 09:35 CET Competing against 36 leading contenders from 20 countries, four Taiwanese children’s choirs have garnered several major awards and top honors at the 5th Budapest International Choral Celebration, showcasing Taiwan’s cultural diversity and music excellence. This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260722613876/en/ Puzangalan Children’s Choir and Yo Wu Wei Children’s Chorus join forces with international choral ensembles and orchestras to perform Mozart’s Requiem Mass in D minor, K. 626 at the Béla Bartók National Concert Hall of Müpa Budapest. With its pure, angelic voices and exceptional vocal techniques, Puzangalan Children’s Choir from Pingtung County won the top prize, Laurea Summa Cum Laude, in the Grand Prix Competition’s Youth Choir of Equal Voices, Folklore, and Sacred Music categories. In the Open Competition, Yo Wu Wei Children’s Chorus claimed three gold prizes in the categories of Youth Choir of Equal Voices, Modern, and Folklore. The choir also secured two championships in the Youth Choir of Equal Voices and Modern categories and received the highest honor in the Modern category. Meanwhile, Taipei Fuhsing Elementary School Choir earned the Children’s Choirs Gold Diploma and was named the Category Winner. Kaohsiung Children’s Choir received a gold prize in the Folklore category and the Children’s Choirs Silver Diploma. Invited by the organizer, Puzangalan Children’s Choir and Yo Wu Wei Children’s Chorus joined forces with international choral ensembles and orchestras to perform Mozart’s Requiem Mass in D minor, K. 626 at the Béla Bartók National Concert Hall of Müpa Budapest. The two choirs then embarked on a tour of the Baltic states, bringing Taiwan’s choral artistry to audiences in Poland, Lithuania, and Latvia while sharing Taiwanese music and culture with local communities. The Taipei Representative Office in Hungary noted that the award-winning achievements at the choral competition demonstrate the confidence of Taiwan’s younger generation on the global stage. It added that the children’s voices have become a powerful form of cultural diplomacy, leaving a lasting impression at this year’s event. https://www.theyeshivaworld.com/news/gen.text: WWII HISTORY: New German Military Base Threatens Historic Jewish Partisan Bunkers In Lithuania August 28, 2026 4:30 pm One Comment The construction of Germany’s first permanent military base outside its borders since World War II is raising concerns over the future of historic bunkers in Lithuania where hundreds of Jews who escaped the Vilna Ghetto hid while fighting the Nazis. The bunkers, located in Lithuania’s Rūdninkai Forest, were used by approximately 400 Jewish partisans and are described as the country’s only memorial site dedicated specifically to Jewish resistance during the Holocaust. Concerns have increased as construction moves forward on a base for Germany’s 45th Armored Brigade. Signs warning of a dangerous military area and prohibiting entry have begun appearing in the forest, making access increasingly difficult for descendants of the Jewish partisans who travel there to visit the historic site. Germany has said it is committed to preserving the former partisan camp as a place of remembrance and education, stressing that the bunkers are not part of the military training facilities. Berlin, however, says responsibility for managing the site and determining public access rests with Lithuanian authorities. Lithuania’s Culture Ministry, meanwhile, says the bunkers do not qualify for protected cultural-heritage status because they are not considered authentic structures. According to the ministry, the bunkers were reconstructed during the Soviet era and were associated with Soviet propaganda. Researchers argue that the position reflects a broader Lithuanian historical narrative that places greater emphasis on Soviet repression and makes recognition of the legacy of Jewish partisans more difficult. Lithuanian officials say visits to the site will eventually be permitted, but visitors will be required to follow military regulations and receive advance approval from the training-area command. Authorities also plan to install a new informational sign near the site. ( YWN World Headquarters – NYC ) One Response The idea that a memorial to Jewish resistance is not “authentic” because it was “reconstructed during the Soviet era” and “associated with Soviet propaganda” is a dangerous form of historical revisionism. The Jewish partisans who fought in the Rūdninkai Forest were heroes, regardless of who rebuilt their bunkers later or what political regime tried to co-opt their memory. Their fight for survival against the Nazis stands on its own merit. We must remember their courage. To diminish their legacy because of Soviet-era politics is to deny a critical part of the Holocaust narrative and, frankly, to insult their memory. We must protect sites like these, not obstruct access to them. Leave a Reply You must be logged in to post a comment. Photograph: Elizabeth Frantz/Reuters View image in fullscreen Ilhan Omar, a frequent target of Donald Trump’s anti-Somali rhetoric, said she would ‘not be silenced’ by the justice department’s investigation. Photograph: Elizabeth Frantz/Reuters Ilhan Omar Ilhan Omar’s phone seized and relatives subpoenaed in criminal inquiry, source says Federal authorities issued more than a dozen grand jury subpoenas in inquiry into potential immigration fraud US politics live – latest updates Associated Press Wed 14 Oct 2026 18.22 EDT Last modified on Wed 14 Oct 2026 19.35 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Federal authorities investigating the Minnesota representative Ilhan Omar seized the Democratic lawmaker’s phone and have issued more than a dozen grand jury subpoenas, including to some of her relatives, according to a person briefed on the inquiry. The subpoenas were issued for a grand jury collecting evidence in Minnesota as federal authorities investigate potential fraud in Omar’s immigration paperwork, said the person, who spoke on the condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to discuss an ongoing investigation. The investigation led to federal agents searching Omar’s Washington DC home on Monday just weeks before the November midterms , in which Omar is seeking re-election. The scope of the investigation into Omar is unclear, though the secretary of the Department of Homeland Security, Markwayne Mullin, has suggested that authorities were examining potential crimes related to her family’s immigration paperwork. Democrats rebuke federal raid of Ilhan Omar’s home: ‘rogue abuse of power’ Read more On Tuesday, Jeanine Pirro, the US attorney for the District of Columbia, said in a Fox News interview that “there are several investigations going on” related to Omar and that her office is also looking into issues concerning the lawmaker’s financial disclosures. “If there was a crime that was committed, it will be prosecuted,” Pirro said. The search of Omar’s home so close to next month’s midterm contests, which will determine control of the House and the Senate, was swiftly condemned by Democrats, who accused the administration of targeting the representative for political purposes. Omar, in a statement on X, called the search an “attempt to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement”. “For 10 years, Trump has targeted me with baseless lies and smear campaigns. This is just the latest escalation in his campaign of political intimidation,” she said. “I will not be silenced.” A phone message seeking comment was left on Wednesday with a representative for Omar. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly, plus breaking news alerts Sign up to The Stakes 2026 A weekly guide to what really matters in the US midterms, plus breaking news alerts. after newsletter promotion Though the Republican focus on Omar’s background dates back years, the search notably took place three weeks before the November midterms, in which Omar is seeking re-election. The justice department has historically sought to avoid public investigative actions involving a candidate within 60 days of a primary or general election. Omar, who was first elected to the House in 2018, represents Minnesota’s fifth district, including Minneapolis. She is part of “the Squad” of progressive lawmakers who are a vibrant political force on the left wing of Congress but have also endured repeated attacks from Trump, dating back to his first term. She was one of the first two Muslim American women in the House and the first African refugee to be elected to Congress.
